Question: Does the capacitance of a capacitor depend upon change and voltage?
Answer: The capacitor’s capacitance is fixed during manufacturing. The unit of Capacitance is Farad. Since Farad has a huge value, the industry generally uses “Micro Farad,” “Pico Farad,” “nano Farad,”” Femto Farad,” etc. However, the Resistance the Capacitor gives varies based on the frequency or the voltage. The resistance given by the Capacitor is called Reactance. The following formula calculates this. Reactance Xc = 1/(2πfC) . C is the value of the Capacitance. f is the frequency. So, if the frequency is higher, the reactance offered by the capacitor is less. If the frequency is less, then the Capacitor’s Reactance is More. Every electrical component has a rating: maximum current or maximum voltage. Capacitors have a voltage rating. The capacitor will be damaged if the applied voltage exceeds the rated voltage.

Question: What is the difference between driver, software, and firmware in embedded systems?
Answer: Driver, Software and Firmware all are Software only. If you run a Software directly on Microprocessor (Bare Metal Programming) then that is called Firmware. If you run a software on top of Operating System then that is called Software. Software function written to access a specific device is called Driver. Example: Display driver, Network driver, Mouse Driver, Keyboard Driver. Firmware uses the driver to interface with the devices.

Answer: Let us start from the basics. Microcontroller = Microprocessor + Memory + Controllers Memory = ROM + RAM Microprocessor can not interfere with the devices directly. It connects with devices through controllers only. For example: Microprocessor -> Display Controller -> Display Microprocessor -> HardDisk Controller -> Harddisk The same way to connect to the Internet Microprocessor uses Network Controller. There are various types of Networks are available. But Ethernet is used to connect with Internet. In Ethernet there are two types. In wired Ethernet you need to connect the Microcontroller will be connected with Internet using wires. This fast. In wireless Ethernet (WiFi) you can connect the Microcontroller with ethernet without wires. But this will be slower than Wired Ethernet.. This WiFi Controller can be integrated inside the Microcontroller or Outside the Microcontroller. Question: What is the difference between Latch And Flip-flop? …
Answer: Latch is Asynchronous. Flip-Flop is Synchronous. For example in RS Latch, if the Value of the R& S changes the output will change. Question: What exactly is a micro controller? What distinguishes a microprocessor from a microcontroller? What are the differences between RISC and CISC microprocessors?
Answer: Microcontroller = Microprocessor + ROM + RAM + Controllers. That is Microprocessor , ROM, RAM and Controllers are build into a Single Chip is called Microcontroller. Microprocessor is nothing but CPU (Central Processing Unit) on a Chip. The Microprocessor Execute instructions like ADD (addition), SUB (Subtractions), MUL (Multiplication), DIV (Divide), AND, OR, NOT, MOV (Move data between local Memory also called as Registers), LD (Load, Move Data from External Memory to Local Register), ST(Store, Move Data from Local Register to External Memory), JMP (Move to any location), CALL (Execute set of instructions and come back), etc. To execute these instructions few steps need to be followed. Based the execution of these steps, the microprocessors are called as RISC or CISC. In CISC Microprocessor these steps are stored in a memory, the Control Unit (CU), read one by one the steps and execute the instruction. This takes more time (Slow execution. But more instructions can be stored in Memory). Complex instructions can be stored in Memory. When high end software need to be executed, Engineers use CISC Microprocessor. In RISK Microprocessor these steps are implemented in Hardware. Since it is implemented in Hardware the execution will be faster (Parallel Execution , not sequential execution - one by one). But when you need more instructions, it need to silicon Space. That is why they have less instruction and called it as Reduced Instruction Set Computer. When High speed and less complex software need to be executed, Engineers use RISC Microprocessor. I share my Embedded Systems Programming course free with the students. Question: What is a general purpose microprocessor?

Question: Why do we use a clock in a microprocessor? What would happen if we don't use it in a microprocessor?
Answer: There are two types of Digital Circuits. In Synchronous Circuits the Clock is used to synchronize the input signals to a block. Let us see an example here. If we 5 friends decided to go for a movie and the movie starts at 6 p.m. We all decided to assemble before the movie theatre by 5:50 p.m. and go into the theatre. Each one of them come at any time 5:20, 5:30, 5:40, 4:46, 5:48, but we will go to inside the theatre by 5:50 p.m. Move starts at 6:00 p.m. This is called synchronous. If we 5 friends decided to go for a movie and the movie starts at 6 p.m., as and when each one comes they get into to the theatre, then it is called Asynchronous. The same thing can used on travel also, when you do public travel like bus, train, plane, ship, etc., everyone comes at fixed time then the journey starts. The advantage of Synchronous predictability. But the disadvantage is waste of time. Some comes early need to wait. No one can come late. But when you handle huge events this is good. Like our public transport. The advantage of Asynchronous event is, it can happen anytime based on their occurrence. But the disadvantage is unpredictability. No one knows when who will come. So large digital circuits are using Synchronous method. They use clock period (one Positive edge to another positive edge) for processing and Clock edge to Synchronize. The event must happen before the positive edge. The Microprocessor is a huge Synchronous digital Circuit. So the clock is used to synchronize all the internal blocks of Microprocessor. If you do not give clock, Microprocessor will not function. Also the speed of the clock should not exceed the speed mentioned by the manufacturer.
